content.title: Where Is the 'Malcolm in the Middle' Cast Now? Inside Their Lives Before Returning for the Reboot
content.text: NEED TO KNOW Malcolm in the Middle ended its original run in May 2006A revival of the sitcom was announced in December 2024, with most of the original cast returningMalcolm in the Middle: Life's Still Unfair premiered April 10 on Hulu and Hulu on Disney+ After 20 years, the Wilkerson family reunion is finally here. In 2006, Malcolm in the Middle ended after seven seasons. Now, the beloved, dysfunctional TV family is returning to the small screen for a revival series on Hulu and Hulu on Disney+. Malcolm in the Middle: Life's Still Unfair, which premiered April 10, saw original cast members Bryan Cranston, Jane Kaczmarek, Frankie Muniz, Christopher Masterson and Justin Berfield reprise their roles. Erik Per Sullivan, who played Dewey, did not return, and his character is played by Caleb Ellsworth-Clark. The revival consists of four episodes. According to the official description, it follows Malcolm and his daughter, Leah, who are "drawn into the family’s chaos when Hal (Cranston) and Lois (Kaczmarek) demand his presence for their 40th wedding anniversary party.” In the years since Malcolm in the Middle ended, the cast members' careers have varied. Cranston has continued acting in series like Breaking Bad, while Muniz has pursued his love of race car driving. So, where is the cast of Malcolm in the Middle now? Here's everything to know about what the sitcom's cast has been up to since viewers last saw them as the Wilkersons. Frankie Muniz as Malcolm Frankie Muniz in 'Malcolm in the Middle' ; Frankie Muniz attends the Mark Wahlberg Youth Foundation Celebrity Invitational Gala on December 02, 2023 in Las Vegas, Nevada. © 20th Century Fox ; Gabe Ginsberg/Getty Muniz played the titular character on the popular sitcom. Over the years, he has appeared on series such as Criminal Minds and Last Man Standing. In addition to acting on-screen, he has hit the dance floor, competing on season 25 of Dancing with the Stars. Muniz has also pursued a career in race car driving. In 2024, he announced he was joining Reaume Brothers Racing as a full-time driver for the 2025 season of the NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series. "I want people to know that I've literally dedicated my life to this," he told PEOPLE in October 2024. "I love it. When I'm not in the race car, I'm thinking about being in the race car." In 2019, Muniz married model Paige Muniz (née Price). After eloping in October 2019, the couple held a formal wedding in February 2020. They later welcomed a son, Mauz Mosley Muniz, in March 2021. In recent years, Muniz has made appearances on several TV shows, including The Rookie, New Amsterdam and Awkwafina Is Nora From Queens. He reprises his role as Malcolm in Malcolm in the Middle: Life's Still Unfair. Jane Kaczmarek as Lois Jane Kaczmarek in 'Malcolm in the Middle' ; Jane Kaczmarek attends the 39th Annual Santa Barbara International Film Festival on February 15, 2024 in Santa Barbara, California. © 20th Century Fox ; Matt Winkelmeyer/Getty Kaczmarek delivered tough love as Lois, the matriarch of the Wilkerson family. At the Emmys, she was nominated for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Comedy Series throughout her entire run on the series — a total of seven times. In 2008, Kaczmarek played Judge Trudy Kessler on the TNT legal drama Raising the Bar. In recent years, she has had roles on This Is Us, Carol's Second Act, Mixed-ish and The Changeling. Kaczmarek returns as Lois in the reboot series. Kaczmarek was married to The Handmaid's Tale actor Bradley Whitford for 16 years, with whom she welcomed three children. The couple filed for divorce in 2009. Bryan Cranston as Hal Bryan Cranston in 'Malcolm in the Middle' ; Bryan Cranston attends "The Studio" Tastemaker Screening on March 26, 2025 in New York City. © 20th Century Fox ; Eric Charbonneau/Apple TV+ via Getty Cranston played Hal, the supportive but immature dad on Malcolm in the Middle. In the almost two decades since Malcolm in the Middle ended, Cranston has acted in a wide array of projects. Two years after the sitcom, he played chemistry teacher-turned-drug-lord Walter White on the critically acclaimed AMC drama Breaking Bad, for which he won a total of six Emmys. Aside from Emmys, Cranston has also won two Tony Awards for Best Leading Actor in a Play, in 2014 and 2019, respectively. Notably, he played Hollywood screenwriter Dalton Trumbo in Trumbo, earning him an Oscar nomination for Best Actor in 2015. Cranston has continued keeping busy, acting in Godzilla, Power Rangers, Isle of Dogs, Asteroid City and The Phoenician Scheme. He starred in both seasons of Your Honor on Showtime and three episodes of Apple TV+'s The Studio. The actor once again plays Hal in the four-episode revival. Cranston has been married to actress Robin Dearden since 1989. The pair share one daughter, Taylor Dearden, who stars in The Pitt. Christopher Masterson as Francis Chris Masterson in 'Malcolm in the Middle' ; Chris Masterson attends HEAVEN 2016 on June 18, 2015 in Los Angeles, California. © 20th Century Fox ; Michael Buckner/Getty Masterson portrayed Francis, the oldest of the Wilkerson brothers. Following the end of Malcolm in the Middle, Masterson made guest appearances on White Collar, Men at Work and Haven. Outside of acting, Masterson has become a DJ. While speaking to A Drink With in August 2012, he said he began dabbling with turntables "five or six years ago." "I started doing it and realized really quickly how much work that it takes to go out and play and not suck," he continued. "I deejayed in my bedroom for two years, literally two years that I’d just be whiling out in my bedroom." Masterson wed Yolanda Pecoraro in August 2019. They announced the arrival of their first child, a daughter named Chiara Darby, in April 2021. The actor reprises his role as Francis in Malcolm in the Middle: Life's Still Unfair. Justin Berfield as Reese Justin Berfield in 'Malcolm in the Middle' ; Justin Berfield attends "Hollywood Virgin" book release party on February 05, 2025 in West Hollywood, California. © 20th Century Fox ; Michael Tullberg/Getty Berfield played Reese, Malcolm's mischievous older brother. Berfield has mostly been behind the camera since his Malcolm days. As Variety reported in November 2010, Berfield and his producing partner, Jason Felts, launched Virgin Produced, a "Los Angeles-based film and television development, packaging and production company." One of his most recent projects was the E! 2022 reality series, Relatively Famous: Ranch Rules, which he was an executive producer on. In his personal life, Berfield has two children. In a May 2025 Instagram post, Berfield posted a series of images from the set of the Malcolm in the Middle revival. "It was so amazing catching up with old friends and meeting some amazing new ones!" he wrote. "We’re so lucky that we got to come back to these characters after 20 years and see where they’ve been." Erik Per Sullivan as Dewey Erik Per Sullivan in 'Malcolm in the Middle' ; Erik Per Sullivan attends the 'Arthur And The Invisibles' film premiere on January 7, 2007 in New York. © 20th Century Fox ; Charles Sykes/Shutterstock Per Sullivan played Dewey, the lovable brother on the series. Per Sullivan appeared in the 2010 Joel Schumacher film, Twelve, starring Chace Crawford and Emma Roberts, but has since left the world of acting. In an April 2024 interview, Kaczmarek, who played his TV mom, said that Per Sullivan was doing "very, very well" and "wasn't interested in acting at all" after Malcolm in the Middle ended. In a June 2025 episode of the Fly on the Wall with Dana Carvey and David Spade podcast, Cranston revealed he spoke with Per Sullivan about the revival, but the former child actor had no interest in returning. "He's really, really smart, and he's getting his master's at Harvard right now," Cranston continued. "He said, 'Oh, God no. I haven't acted since I was 9 or something, so I'm not into it.' " In April 2026, Kaczmarek echoed Cranston's sentiments, telling The Guardian, “He’s studying Dickens and is an incredible student," adding that Malcolm producers "offered him buckets of money to come back, and he just said: ‘No thank you.' "
